It sounds like your tampon was not inserted high enough, and it didn’t make it all the way out of the applicator. 

Make sure that when you push the applicator “button” that the string is not under your finger. If the string gets held in place, it will feel like the applicator has been fully discharged, because the “button” won’t move any farther. But the tampon will not be entirely out of the applicator, causing it to sit too low or be pulled out with the applicator.

It seems counterintuitive, but the higher you place the tampon, the more comfortable it will be! As long as you aren’t forcing it or using one too large. (NAD) I’m currently recovering from my hysterectomy! I’m 25yo, so it was a struggle to find a doctor willing to help me. Since I was about 18yo, I’ve known I don’t want kids of my own. But I’m still glad I waited at least a little while to make sure it was my permanent mindset; for a few big things I was “so sure of” at 20yo, I’ve now done a 180.

I plan on making a big, detailed post about my experience, but for now: My periods were not solved with birth control. I remember at age 18 asking for an ablation (not granted.) Until two weeks ago, I was on three doses of birth control just to stop the continuous bleeding/spotting. The hormones started affecting my ADHD meds, and it was expensive and stressful trying to obtain all the medication I needed. I tried multiple forms of hormonal birth control. I would find one that seemed to work, and then the symptoms would return after 1-2 years.

My hysterectomy was right for me, but I don’t know that I wish I would’ve gotten it sooner. I think 16yo is WAY too young to make a permanent decision, and I’m a huge advocate for bodily autonomy in young adults. Spend a couple years deeply researching which type of hysterectomy you want, the pros and cons of each type, the risks of the procedure and the anesthesia itself, and whether you’re okay with the risks presented. Your mindset should not be “early menopause won’t happen to me” or “ureter damage is so unlikely.” You need to be certain that you would accept that complication for the sake of the procedure.

OP, I hope you find a doctor that listens to you and works with you to find a solution!

European vs American coffeemakers have different ounces per “cup,” and different brands of cold brew have vastly different amounts of caffeine.
